verdict.rationale: RustDesk documents running its rendezvous/relay servers on your own infrastructure, with P2P sessions falling back to your own relay, so users decide where server-side data and traffic live. Community reports confirm working self-hosted deployments, though some found setup difficult and worried about the default relays' location. Residency is achieved only through self-hosting, not an explicit region-selection or data-residency feature. Missing for 10: an explicit data-residency or region choice for vendor-hosted service, and documentation of what data each server stores and where.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can choose where my data is stored (region/residency)

citations.quote: a secure and reliable remote desktop experience with your own self-hosted servers
You can use our rendezvous/relay server, set up your own, or write your own rendezvous/relay server.
clients connect peer to peer when they can and fall back to your relay.
